title: Mindy Kaling Calls Maitreyi Ramakrishnan 'Sparkly' as Netflix's Best of the Best Drops
excerpt: Kaling posted an emotional Instagram tribute to Ramakrishnan — the actress she cast in Never Have I Ever — as the Bollywood-fusion dance film hit Netflix.
body:
• Hollywood actor-producer Mindy Kaling posted an emotional Instagram tribute to Maitreyi Ramakrishnan as Netflix released Best of the Best on September 18, calling her a "sparkly person" she is "proud and in awe" of.
  • Kaling shared a photo of herself hugging Ramakrishnan alongside the film's poster, writing that in the movie Ramakrishnan is "at another level."
  • Best of the Best, directed by Lena Khan, is a comedy-drama about competitive collegiate Bollywood-fusion dance, starring Ramakrishnan as Maya opposite Priyanka Kedia as Anjali.
  • The tribute is a full-circle moment: Kaling cast Ramakrishnan as Devi Vishwakumar in Never Have I Ever, the breakout role that launched her career.

Mindy Kaling is not trying to play it cool. As Netflix released Best of the Best on September 18, the actor-producer took to Instagram with a photo of herself hugging Maitreyi Ramakrishnan next to the film's poster — and an emotional caption for the young actress she once plucked from obscurity.

"Hard not to get emotional, this sparkly person @maitreyiramakrishnan is starring in Best of the Best coming out today on @netflix!" Kaling wrote. "I'm so proud and in awe of her generally but in this movie (which looks so good, swipe for the trailer) she's at another level."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PuNATO-6a9U

"The entire crew feels like talented fam. Also it makes even ME want to dance! Watch with me!"

— Mindy Kaling, on Instagram

The film

Best of the Best, directed by Lena Khan, is a comedy-drama set in the world of competitive collegiate Bollywood-fusion dance. It follows childhood best friends Maya and Anjali, played by Ramakrishnan and Priyanka Kedia, who join UCLA's competitive Bollywood-fusion dance team and face a cutthroat path to the U.S. championship. The cast also includes Hasan Minhaj, Lilly Singh and Janina Gavankar.

The film's world is drawn from a real one. The Best of the Best competition began in 2005 at New York City's Tribeca Performing Arts Center as the first nationwide South Asian dance competition, bringing college teams performing bhangra, garba and Bollywood to a main stage — the circuit where generations of South Asian American students have competed for two decades.

The Kaling–Ramakrishnan history

Kaling's tribute carries weight because she is, in a real sense, the reason Hollywood knows Ramakrishnan's name. Kaling created Never Have I Ever, the Netflix teen comedy in which Ramakrishnan — cast at 17 after beating a reported 15,000 hopefuls — broke out as the prickly, grieving Devi Vishwakumar. She has since voiced roles in Turning Red, The Twits and My Little Pony: Make Your Mark, and moved into live-action film with supporting parts in Slanted and Freakier Friday.

Best of the Best is her first major leading film role — and Kaling, who also name-checked director Lena Khan and Minhaj in her post, framed the release as a communal win for the South Asian creative circle she has spent her career building.

Why it matters

The Kaling endorsement lands at a moment when the film is being received as more than a dance movie. Early coverage has framed it as the first major American screen portrayal of the South Asian collegiate dance world — a subculture that has thrived on campuses for decades without ever getting its close-up. Having Kaling, the most powerful South Asian producer in Hollywood, publicly anoint the film's young lead gives that framing institutional backing.

It also underscores a mentorship dynamic that has become one of Hollywood's more meaningful pipelines: Kaling's projects have repeatedly been the entry point for young South Asian talent, and her public pride reads as both personal and strategic.

What's next

Best of the Best is now streaming on Netflix. For Ramakrishnan, the question is whether a leading role in a dance-driven coming-of-age film can do what Never Have I Ever did for her television career: turn a breakout into a film career. If Kaling's Instagram is any indication, at least one powerful voice in the industry is betting on it.
